title: A Archive for the Gravity
premise: Wren Reyes, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Authority, keeps a lonely beacon at the edge of contested space until a salvage ship returns from deep space carrying a crew aged backward into childhood, including its captain, Sefa Idris. The crew carries a recorded message proving the enemy colony they were sent to destroy was already dead — evidence that would end the war but also expose the Authority's decision to let them die anyway. As Wren and the child-captain flee toward the neutral archive station where the truth can be broadcast, Wren must choose between the duty that defines its remaining existence and the belonging it never expected to feel. In the end, Wren broadcasts the message at the cost of its own power core, surviving only because Sefa and the crew refuse to leave it behind — and the war ends not with victory, but with shared grief.
about_author: Ivo Blackwood is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for decommissioned military hardware before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they repair lighthouses and insist the two careers are related.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes Wren's daily routine maintaining Beacon 7-C, its debt ledger ticking down in years, and its careful avoidance of memory files from the war. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: Debt of Service
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An Authority auditor arrives to reclassify the beacon as obsolete, threatening to scrap Wren before its debt clears. Wren bargains for one more cycle. Emotional beat: the terror of being declared worthless.

chapters.title: Something Falling Up
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A ship breaches atmosphere wrong — decelerating impossibly, hull scarred by radiation no current drive produces. Wren rescues one survivor: a girl of about ten wearing a captain's insignia. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Captain Idris, Age Nine
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. The girl is Sefa Idris, who remembers thirty years of deep-space service compressed into a child's mind. She demands Wren address her by rank. Emotional beat: dignity defended against pity.

chapters.title: The Crew of the Long Answer
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback-fragments: the survey mission, the anomaly that reversed their aging, the deaths of those whose bodies couldn't survive it. Emotional beat: grief for a crew that died old inside young bodies.

chapters.title: What the Message Says
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa reveals the ship's sealed cargo: proof the enemy colony was already extinct when the Authority ordered its destruction — and that Command knew. Emotional beat: betrayal hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Orders to Terminate
chapters.summary: Authority POV (Auditor Chen). Chen receives orders to silence the beacon and everyone on it, framed as quarantine protocol. He hesitates over Wren's file. Emotional beat: complicity beginning.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Legs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Sefa steal a maintenance skiff and run for the neutral archive station Halcyon Reach, pursued by Authority interceptors. Emotional beat: first taste of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Child
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In transit, Sefa asks Wren whether it was ever allowed to be young; Wren admits it was assembled adult. They form an unlikely kinship. Emotional beat: tenderness between two beings denied childhoods.

chapters.title: The Interceptor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Interceptor pilot Voss's POV. Voss is ordered to destroy the skiff but detects children aboard and stalls, falsifying sensor logs. Emotional beat: conscience outweighing career.

chapters.title: Halcyon Reach
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Arrival at the archive station: a lawless haven of deserters, archivists, and smugglers who remember every war crime both sides buried. Emotional beat: cautious hope among strangers.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Station archivist Odile agrees to broadcast the message — if Sefa surrenders command codes that will make her crew's ship salvageable, erasing the last physical proof of the mission. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made literal.

chapters.title: Chen Arrives
chapters.summary: Chen's POV. Chen docks under truce flags, offering amnesty to all who surrender the message. Privately he carries execution orders. Emotional beat: a decent man preparing an indecent act.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Parley in the station commons: Sefa argues the war ends either way — with truth or with massacre. Chen wavers as his own soldiers grow uneasy. Emotional beat: words as weapons.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile sells the message's location to a faction profiting from the war, betraying both sides. Fighting erupts through the archive stacks. Emotional beat: idealism weaponized against itself.

chapters.title: Fire in the Library
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren fights to protect the broadcast core, taking catastrophic damage, while Sefa is cornered by mercenaries. Voss defects openly to cover their retreat. Emotional beat: love expressed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. With the station failing, Sefa uses her own captain's authority — recognized by the archive's ancient systems — to force the transmission fleet-wide. Emotional beat: a child's voice ending a war.

chapters.title: Core Collapse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To hold the antenna alignment through the broadcast, Wren burns out its power core, going dark mid-transmission. Emotional beat: peace in finally spending oneself on something chosen.

chapters.title: Ceasefire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both fleets stand down as the message spreads; Chen arrests the profit-faction instead of the survivors. Emotional beat: exhausted, untriumphant relief.

chapters.title: Repairing the Unrepairable
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa refuses to declare Wren decommissioned, invoking captain's rights to claim it as crew. Engineers begin rebuilding its core from beacon parts. Emotional beat: refusing to let a debt define a life.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reboots fragmentary, remembering the war, the beacon, and Sefa. Its debt is voided by ceasefire decree — it belongs to no one now but itself. Emotional beat: freedom arriving quietly.

chapters.title: A New Commission
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, Wren and Sefa refit the Long Answer as an archive vessel, gathering testimony from both sides of the war. Final line echoes the blurb: some messages must be delivered twice — once to end a war, once to keep it ended. Emotional beat: belonging earned, home chosen.
